svg.metadata: {"concept_id": "edu.sand-dollar-test-upper-surface", "profiles": ["swell-paper-v1", "index-embossed-v1", "viewplus-variable-height-v1"], "teaching": "Introduced aboral surface of a dried sand-dollar test using a regularised Echinarachnius parma anatomical example: continuous flattened disc with five petaloid ambulacral regions and no lunules. NOAA1985technical identification key and full Figure31page were inspected; selectedE.parma has no lunules, five petaloid surface fields and a peripheral posterior periproct. Tiny genital/periproct anatomy omitted because this is a sparse upper-test lesson; four gonopores are not drawn as five central holes. The primary figure has varied plating/petal detail, not five literally identical curves. Our regularised enlarged model is not a traced specimen or complete diagnostic morphology. Native1036outer marks/source identity remains an exact-source-fit appendix issue, not silently covered by a no-lunule model.
